correctness.rationale: At every interior simple zero S there is a C2 inverse coordinate s=S(t); the density derivative is (w'S'-w S'')/|S'|^3. The odd smoothing defect has exact first moment r sqrt(r²+δ)-r²-δ asinh(r/sqrtδ)=-(δ/2)log(1/δ)+O(δ). The quadratic inverse-density remainder and the away-zero region integrate to O(δ); the absolute defect integrates to 2sqrtδ/|S'| plus O(δlog(1/δ)) per zero. Closed-form double-integrator integrals independently reproduce the sharp 1/2 position coefficient. 37 65-digit numerical checks passed; no finite check is used as proof.

value.rationale: The normalized-algebraic surrogate is used in indirect optimal-control shooting. Its algebraic tails produce a sharp delta log(1/delta) weak bias that differs both from the sqrt(delta) control L1 error and the O(delta) terminal velocity response. The local coefficient exposes when this harmful term cancels; the double-integrator terminal-position coefficient 1/2 holds for any interior switch, giving a natural, non-arbitrary benchmark for continuation tolerances and terminal-state accuracy. No algorithm-sized contribution is assumed.
